references.text: Eli says to Hannah, 'Go in peace' (לְכִי לְשָׁלוֹם) – the same closing pattern Jesus uses here: a blessing of peace after faith and prayer have been answered.

Jesus says to the woman with the issue of blood, 'Your faith has saved you. Go in peace' (ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε· πορεύου εἰς εἰρήνην) – almost identical wording, linking faith, salvation, and peace.
Jesus says to blind Bartimaeus, 'Your faith has saved you' (ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε). The same expression is used to confirm that faith is the cause of salvation/healing.
Jesus says to the woman with the issue of blood in Luke's version: 'Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.' Identical phrasing as in Luke 7:50, showing this is a recurring statement from Jesus.
Jesus says to the Samaritan leper, 'Your faith has saved you' – again using the same formulation about faith as a saving power.
Jesus says to the blind man at Jericho, 'Your faith has saved you.' Once more the same expression confirming the connection between faith and salvation.
Jesus says to the woman with the issue of blood, 'Your faith has saved you' (ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε). Matthew's version of the same statement about the saving power of faith.
Paul writes that it is by grace you have been saved through faith. This expresses the same theological principle Jesus formulates in Luke 7:50 – salvation through faith.
Habakkuk 2:4 says that 'the righteous shall live by his faith' – a fundamental Old Testament principle about the importance of faith, which underlies Jesus' words that her faith has saved her.
The immediate context where Jesus forgives the woman's sins and links her love to forgiveness. Verse 50 summarizes and confirms that faith is the basis for salvation.
